title: PR #41794 — Tweens are no longer nodes (fire and forget)

blocks.text:
Tweens are no longer nodes. They are References, with very similar logic
to SceneTreeTimers, designed in a "fire and forget" manner. You create a
Tween with get_tree().create_tween(), which results in an empty Tween.
tween_property is the equivalent of the old interpolate_property;
tween_interval waits (a timer); tween_callback is interpolate_callback;
tween_method is interpolate_method. You can call as many tweening methods
as you want; they are sequenced one after another. Parallel tweening is
explicit via a dedicated method. Tweens are intended for fire-and-forget
use: create_tween() inside a Node automatically binds the Tween, and
bind_node(node) makes the Tween skip processing when the node is not in
the tree and removes it when the node is freed. You can stop (reset),
pause, resume and kill a Tween.
